component.name: openai
component.title: OpenAI
component.description: OpenAI endpoint for chat completion, Responses API, embeddings, audio transcription, audio translation, and text-to-speech.
component.label: ai

apiKey.description: Default API key for all endpoints

audioModel.description: Default model for audio transcription endpoints

baseUrl.description: Default base URL for all endpoints

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

model.description: Default model for chat completion endpoints

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

useGlobalSslContextParameters.label: security
useGlobalSslContextParameters.description: Enable usage of global SSL context parameters

CamelOpenAIUserMessage.description: The user message to send to the OpenAI chat completion API

CamelOpenAISystemMessage.description: The system message to provide context and instructions to the model

CamelOpenAIDeveloperMessage.description: The developer message to provide additional instructions to the model

CamelOpenAIModel.description: The model to use for chat completion

CamelOpenAITemperature.description: Controls randomness in the response. Higher values (e.g., 0.8) make output more random, lower values (e.g., 0.2) make it more deterministic

CamelOpenAITopP.description: An alternative to temperature for controlling randomness. Uses nucleus sampling where the model considers tokens with top_p probability mass

CamelOpenAIMaxTokens.description: The maximum number of tokens to generate in the completion

CamelOpenAIPreviousResponseId.description: Previous response id for server-side conversation state on the Responses API

CamelOpenAIStreaming.description: Whether to stream the response back incrementally

CamelOpenAIOutputClass.description: The Java class name (FQCN) to use for structured output parsing

CamelOpenAIJsonSchema.description: The JSON schema to use for structured output validation

CamelOpenAIStripThinking.description: Whether to strip ... blocks from the response body

CamelOpenAIMediaType.description: The MIME type of the message body when sending a file or binary content (File, WrappedFile, byte or InputStream) to the model. Takes precedence over component content-type headers and automatic MIME type detection

CamelOpenAIThinkingContent.description: The thinking content extracted from ... blocks in the model response

CamelOpenAIReasoningContent.description: The reasoning content from the model response reasoning_content field, used by thinking models like Qwen3 and DeepSeek-R1

CamelOpenAIResponseModel.description: The model used for the completion response

CamelOpenAIResponseId.description: The unique identifier for the completion response

CamelOpenAIFinishReason.description: The reason the completion finished (e.g., stop, length, content_filter)

CamelOpenAIPromptTokens.description: The number of tokens used in the prompt for the latest API call

CamelOpenAICompletionTokens.description: The number of tokens used in the completion for the latest API call

CamelOpenAITotalTokens.description: The total number of tokens used (prompt completion) for the latest API call

CamelOpenAIToolIterations.description: Number of tool call iterations performed in the agentic loop

CamelOpenAIMcpToolCalls.description: List of tool names called during the agentic loop

CamelOpenAIMcpReturnDirect.description: Whether the response came directly from a tool with returnDirect=true, rather than from the LLM

CamelOpenAIAgenticPromptTokens.description: Cumulative prompt tokens consumed across all agentic loop iterations

CamelOpenAIAgenticCompletionTokens.description: Cumulative completion tokens consumed across all agentic loop iterations

CamelOpenAIAgenticTotalTokens.description: Cumulative total tokens consumed across all agentic loop iterations

CamelOpenAIResponse.description: The complete OpenAI chat completion response object

CamelOpenAIResponsesResponse.description: The complete OpenAI Responses API response object

CamelOpenAIModerationResponse.description: The complete OpenAI moderation response object

CamelOpenAIImageResponse.description: The complete OpenAI image generation or edit response object

CamelOpenAIEmbeddingsResponse.description: The complete OpenAI embeddings response object

CamelOpenAIAudioTranscriptionResponse.description: The complete OpenAI audio transcription response object

CamelOpenAIAudioTranslationResponse.description: The complete OpenAI audio translation response object

CamelOpenAIEmbeddingModel.description: The model to use for embeddings

CamelOpenAIEmbeddingResponseModel.description: The embedding model used in the response

CamelOpenAIReferenceEmbedding.description: Reference embedding vector for similarity comparison

CamelOpenAIOriginalText.description: Original text content when embeddings operation is used

CamelOpenAIModerationModel.description: The model to use for moderation (e.g., omni-moderation-latest)

CamelOpenAIModerationFlagged.description: Whether the moderation API flagged the input as violating the usage policies. For a batch of inputs this is true when at least one input was flagged

CamelOpenAIModerationResults.description: One verdict per moderated input, in the order of the inputs. Each entry holds the keys 'input', 'flagged', 'categories' and 'categoryScores', so a batch can be split and routed per item

CamelOpenAIModerationCategories.description: The moderation categories and whether each one was violated, for a single input. Not set for a list body, where 'CamelOpenAIModerationResults' carries the verdicts

CamelOpenAIModerationCategoryScores.description: The moderation confidence score per category, for a single input. Not set for a list body, where 'CamelOpenAIModerationResults' carries the verdicts

CamelOpenAIModerationResponseModel.description: The moderation model used in the response

CamelOpenAIAudioModel.description: The model to use for audio transcription

CamelOpenAIAudioLanguage.description: The language of the input audio (ISO-639-1)

CamelOpenAIAudioResponseFormat.description: The response format for audio transcription (json, text, srt, verbose_json, vtt)

CamelOpenAIAudioTemperature.description: Sampling temperature for audio transcription (0.0 to 1.0)

CamelOpenAIAudioPrompt.description: Optional text to guide the model's style or continue a previous audio segment

CamelOpenAIAudioTimestampGranularities.description: Comma-separated timestamp granularities: word, segment, or word,segment (verbose_json only)

CamelOpenAIAudioDuration.description: Duration of the audio in seconds (verbose_json only)

CamelOpenAIAudioDetectedLanguage.description: Language detected in the audio (verbose_json only)

CamelOpenAISpeechModel.description: The model to use for text-to-speech (e.g., gpt-4o-mini-tts, tts-1, tts-1-hd)

CamelOpenAISpeechVoice.description: The voice to use for the generated audio (e.g., alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, shimmer)

CamelOpenAISpeechResponseFormat.description: The audio format for text-to-speech output (mp3, opus, aac, flac, wav, pcm)

CamelOpenAISpeechSpeed.description: The speed of the generated audio (0.25 to 4.0, where 1.0 is normal speed)

CamelOpenAISpeechInstructions.description: Optional instructions to control the voice of the generated audio (does not work with tts-1 or tts-1-hd)

CamelOpenAIImageModel.description: The model to use for image generation or editing (e.g., gpt-image-1, dall-e-3, dall-e-2)

CamelOpenAIImagePrompt.description: The prompt describing the image to generate, or the edit to apply. Takes precedence over the imagePrompt endpoint option and, for image-generation, over the message body

CamelOpenAIImageSize.description: The size of the generated image (e.g., 1024x1024, 1536x1024, auto)

CamelOpenAIImageQuality.description: The quality of the generated image (auto, high, medium, low for GPT image models; hd, standard for dall-e-3; standard for dall-e-2)

CamelOpenAIImageResponseFormat.description: The response format of the generated image (url or b64_json). Only supported by dall-e-2 and dall-e-3; GPT image models always return base64

CamelOpenAIImageCount.description: The number of images to generate

CamelOpenAIImageBackground.description: The background of the generated image (transparent, opaque, auto). Only supported by GPT image models

CamelOpenAIImageOutputFormat.description: The output format of the generated image (png, jpeg, webp). Only supported by GPT image models

CamelOpenAIImageOutputCompression.description: The compression level (0-100) for the webp or jpeg output formats. Only supported by GPT image models

CamelOpenAIImageStyle.description: The style of the generated image (vivid or natural). Only supported by dall-e-3

CamelOpenAIImageModeration.description: The content moderation level for image generation (low or auto). Only supported by GPT image models

CamelOpenAIImageInputFidelity.description: How closely the edit must match the style and features of the input image (high or low). Only supported by the image-edit operation on gpt-image-1 and gpt-image-1.5

CamelOpenAIImageMask.description: An optional PNG mask for the image-edit operation, where the fully transparent areas indicate where the image should be edited

CamelOpenAIImageResultCount.description: The number of images returned in the response

CamelOpenAIImageRevisedPrompt.description: The prompt as revised by the model, when a single image is returned (dall-e-3)

CamelOpenAIImageRevisedPrompts.description: The prompts as revised by the model, one entry per returned image (dall-e-3)

CamelOpenAIImageInputTokens.description: The number of input tokens billed for the image request. Only reported by GPT image models

CamelOpenAIImageOutputTokens.description: The number of output tokens billed for the image request. Only reported by GPT image models

CamelOpenAIImageTotalTokens.description: The total number of tokens billed for the image request. Only reported by GPT image models

additionalBodyProperty.description: Additional JSON properties to include in the request body (e.g. additionalBodyProperty.traceId=123). This is a multi-value option with prefix: additionalBodyProperty.

additionalHeader.description: Additional HTTP request headers to send with every API call (e.g. additionalHeader.OpenAI-Organization=my-org or additionalHeader.api-key=secret). Values may contain secrets. This is a multi-value option with prefix: additionalHeader.

additionalResponseHeader.description: Map additional fields from the response message to Camel headers. The key is the field name in the API response, the value is the Camel header name (e.g. additionalResponseHeader.reasoning_content=CamelMyReasoningHeader). This is a multi-value option with prefix: additionalResponseHeader.

apiKey.description: OpenAI API key. Can also be set via OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable.

audioLanguage.description: The language of the input audio in ISO-639-1 format (e.g., 'en'). Improves accuracy and latency.

audioModel.description: The model to use for audio transcription (e.g., whisper-1, gpt-4o-transcribe)

audioPrompt.description: Optional text to guide the model's style or continue a previous audio segment

audioResponseFormat.description: The format of the transcription output

audioTimestampGranularities.description: Comma-separated timestamp granularities: 'word', 'segment', or 'word,segment'. Only applicable with verbose_json response format.

autoToolExecution.description: When true and MCP servers are configured, automatically execute tool calls and loop back to the model. When false, tool calls are returned as the message body for manual handling.

baseUrl.description: Base URL for OpenAI API. Defaults to OpenAI's official endpoint. Can be used for local or third-party providers.

builtinTools.description: Comma-separated hosted tools for the Responses API: web_search, file_search, code_interpreter

connectTimeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds for establishing the TCP connection to the API. A connect timeout means the endpoint was unreachable, so the request never ran and is safe to retry. When 0 or negative, the SDK default (1 minute) is used.

conversationHistoryProperty.description: Exchange property name for storing conversation history

developerMessage.description: Developer message to prepend before user messages

dimensions.description: Number of dimensions for the embedding output. Only supported by text-embedding-3 models. Reducing dimensions can lower costs and improve performance without significant quality loss.

embeddingModel.description: The model to use for embeddings

encodingFormat.description: The format for embedding output: 'float' for list of floats, 'base64' for compressed format

fileSearchVectorStoreIds.description: Comma-separated vector store ids required when builtinTools includes file_search

hallucinatedToolNameStrategy.description: Strategy for handling tool names hallucinated by the model (tool not found in any MCP server). 'failExchange' (default) throws an IllegalStateException, failing the exchange immediately. 'repromptModel' sends a corrective tool result listing the available tools so the model can self-correct and retry. The maxToolIterations option bounds retries.

hostedMcpTools.description: JSON array of hosted MCP tool definitions (OpenAI Tool.Mcp) passed through to the Responses API

imageBackground.description: The background of the generated image. Only supported by the GPT image models, and a transparent background requires the png or webp output format.

imageCount.description: The number of images to generate, between 1 and 10. dall-e-3 only supports 1.

imageInputFidelity.description: How closely the edit must match the style and features of the input image. Only supported by the image-edit operation on gpt-image-1 and gpt-image-1.5.

imageModel.description: The model to use for image generation or editing (e.g., gpt-image-1, gpt-image-1-mini, gpt-image-1.5, gpt-image-2). Required for the image-generation and image-edit operations, because the model determines which of the other image options are accepted. The DALL-E models are no longer offered by OpenAI, but remain valid values for OpenAI-compatible providers.

imageModeration.description: The content moderation level applied to image generation. Only supported by the GPT image models.

imageOutputCompression.description: The compression level from 0 to 100 for the webp and jpeg output formats. Only supported by the GPT image models.

imageOutputFormat.description: The output format of the generated image. Only supported by the GPT image models, which default to png.

imagePrompt.description: The prompt describing the image to generate, or the edit to apply. For image-generation the message body is used when this is not set; for image-edit the body carries the input image, so the prompt must come from this option or from the CamelOpenAIImagePrompt header.

imageQuality.description: The quality of the generated image. GPT image models accept auto, high, medium and low; hd and standard are DALL-E values kept for OpenAI-compatible providers.

imageResponseFormat.description: The response format of the generated image. The OpenAI images endpoint rejects this option: the GPT image models always return base64, and the DALL-E models that used to accept it are no longer offered. It is only sent when explicitly set, and is kept for OpenAI-compatible providers that still implement the older images API.

imageSize.description: The size of the generated image (e.g., 1024x1024, 1536x1024, 1024x1536, auto). The accepted values depend on the model.

imageStyle.description: The style of the generated image. A dall-e-3 option, so only useful with OpenAI-compatible providers.

jsonSchema.description: JSON schema for structured output validation

maxAgenticTokens.description: Maximum cumulative prompt plus completion tokens allowed across the MCP agentic loop. When 0 or negative, no token budget is enforced. Enforcement runs after each API call that requests further tool execution, so actual spend may exceed the configured budget by up to one call (typically the largest, as the prompt grows each iteration). A final text response is returned even when cumulative usage exceeds the budget.

maxHistoryMessages.description: When conversationMemory is enabled, retain at most this many messages in the exchange conversation history. System and developer messages are prepended separately and are not stored in history. Assistant tool-call blocks are kept intact and may retain slightly more than this limit to preserve tool result pairing. When 0, no message limit is applied.

maxHistoryTokens.description: When conversationMemory is enabled, trim conversation history using a token estimate (character count / 4, including image payload size for multi-modal user messages). Oldest segments are dropped first until the estimated tokens are within this limit. Assistant tool-call blocks are removed as a unit with their tool results. The most recent segment is always retained, even when it alone exceeds this limit. When 0, no token limit is applied.

maxRetries.description: Maximum number of times the OpenAI SDK client retries failed requests. The SDK retry is rate-limit aware (honors Retry-After on 429).

maxTokens.description: Maximum number of tokens to generate

maxToolIterations.description: Maximum number of tool call loop iterations to prevent infinite loops

mcpProtocolVersions.description: Comma-separated list of MCP protocol versions to advertise when connecting to MCP servers using Streamable HTTP transport. When not set, the SDK default is used. Example: 2024-11-05,2025-03-26,2025-06-18

mcpReconnect.description: Automatically reconnect to MCP servers when a tool call fails due to a transport error, and retry the call once.

mcpServer.description: MCP (Model Context Protocol) server configurations. Define servers using prefix notation: mcpServer..transportType=stdiossestreamableHttp, (Note that sse is deprecated) mcpServer..command= (stdio), mcpServer..args= (stdio), mcpServer..url= (sse/streamableHttp), mcpServer..oauthProfile= (OAuth profile for HTTP auth, requires camel-oauth), mcpServer..toolNames= (optional include list to restrict which tools are registered from this server). This is a multi-value option with prefix: mcpServer.

mcpTimeout.description: Timeout in seconds for MCP tool call requests. Applies to all MCP operations including tool execution and initialization.

mcpToolRefresh.description: Refresh the advertised tool list when an MCP server notifies that its tools changed. Set to false to keep the tool list fixed to what was listed when the endpoint started, for deployments that require a deterministic set of tools.

model.description: The model to use for chat completion

moderationModel.description: The model to use for moderation

outputClass.description: Fully qualified class name for structured output using response format

parallelToolExecution.description: Execute the tool calls returned by the model in a single response concurrently instead of sequentially. Tool calls in the same batch are independent by design, so this reduces the latency of a batch to that of its slowest tool. Results are always fed back to the model in the original tool call order. Note that with toolExecutionErrorStrategy=failExchange the sibling tool calls already dispatched complete before the exchange fails.

parallelToolTimeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds for a batch of parallel tool calls, so that one slow tool cannot block the whole batch. The timeout applies to the batch as a whole, not per tool call. A tool call that exceeds it is cancelled and handled according to toolExecutionErrorStrategy. The default of 0 disables the batch timeout and relies on mcpTimeout, which already bounds each individual MCP request. Only used when parallelToolExecution=true.

previousResponseId.description: Previous response id for OpenAI server-side conversation state (Responses API only)

readTimeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds for reading the response. A read timeout means the model was slow mid-generation, so the request may have been processed. When 0 or negative, requestTimeout applies.

requestTimeout.description: Overall HTTP request timeout in milliseconds for the OpenAI SDK client. When 0 or negative, the SDK default (10 minutes) is used. Acts as the fallback for readTimeout and writeTimeout when those are not set.

speechInstructions.description: Optional instructions to control the voice of the generated audio. Does not work with tts-1 or tts-1-hd.

speechModel.description: The model to use for text-to-speech (e.g., gpt-4o-mini-tts, tts-1, tts-1-hd)

speechResponseFormat.description: The audio format for text-to-speech output

speechSpeed.description: The speed of the generated audio, from 0.25 to 4.0 where 1.0 is normal speed

speechVoice.description: The voice to use for text-to-speech (e.g., alloy, echo, fable, onyx, nova, shimmer). See the OpenAI documentation for the full list of supported voices.

storeFullResponse.description: Store the full SDK response in non-streaming mode: chat-completion uses exchange property 'CamelOpenAIResponse'; responses uses 'CamelOpenAIResponsesResponse'; moderation uses 'CamelOpenAIModerationResponse'; image-generation and image-edit use 'CamelOpenAIImageResponse'; embeddings uses 'CamelOpenAIEmbeddingsResponse'; audio transcription uses 'CamelOpenAIAudioTranscriptionResponse'; audio translation uses 'CamelOpenAIAudioTranslationResponse'

stripThinking.description: Strip ... blocks from model responses (used by reasoning models like Qwen3, DeepSeek-R1). The thinking content is stored in the CamelOpenAIThinkingContent header.

systemMessage.description: System message to prepend. When set and conversationMemory is enabled, the conversation history is reset.

tags.description: Comma-separated tags for discovering route-based tools registered via the ai-tool component. When set, matching tools from the shared AiToolRegistry are exposed to the model alongside MCP tools.

toolExecutionErrorStrategy.description: Strategy for handling exceptions thrown during MCP tool execution. 'failExchange' (default) propagates the exception to the Camel exchange so that standard Camel error handling (onException, dead-letter channel) can process it. This is the safer default because 'repromptModel' sends raw exception messages (which may contain connection strings, hostnames, or internal paths) to a third-party LLM provider. 'repromptModel' catches the error and sends it back to the model as a tool result so the model can attempt to recover.

topP.description: Top P for response generation (0.0 to 1.0)

userMessage.description: Default user message text to use when no prompt is provided

writeTimeout.description: Timeout in milliseconds for writing the request body, which matters for large payloads such as audio and image uploads. When 0 or negative, requestTimeout applies.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

oauthProfile.label: security
oauthProfile.description: OAuth profile name for obtaining an access token via the OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials grant. When set, the token is acquired from the configured identity provider and used instead of apiKey. Requires camel-oauth on the classpath. The profile properties are resolved from camel.oauth..client-id, camel.oauth..client-secret, and camel.oauth..token-endpoint.

sslContextParameters.label: security
sslContextParameters.description: SSLContextParameters to use for configuring SSL/TLS. When set, takes precedence over the individual sslTruststore, sslKeystore, and sslProtocol options.

sslEndpointAlgorithm.label: security
sslEndpointAlgorithm.description: The endpoint identification algorithm to validate the server hostname using the server certificate. Set to an empty string or 'none' to disable hostname verification

sslKeymanagerAlgorithm.label: security
sslKeymanagerAlgorithm.description: The algorithm used by the key manager factory for SSL connections

sslKeyPassword.label: security
sslKeyPassword.description: The password of the private key in the key store file

sslKeystoreLocation.label: security
sslKeystoreLocation.description: The location of the key store file. This is optional and can be used for two-way authentication for the OpenAI API

sslKeystorePassword.label: security
sslKeystorePassword.description: The store password for the key store file

sslKeystoreType.label: security
sslKeystoreType.description: The file format of the key store file

sslProtocol.label: security
sslProtocol.description: The SSL protocol used to generate the SSLContext

sslTrustmanagerAlgorithm.label: security
sslTrustmanagerAlgorithm.description: The algorithm used by the trust manager factory for SSL connections

sslTruststoreLocation.label: security
sslTruststoreLocation.description: The location of the trust store file, used to validate the server's certificate

sslTruststorePassword.label: security
sslTruststorePassword.description: The password for the trust store file. If a password is not set, the configured trust store can still be used, but integrity checking is disabled

sslTruststoreType.label: security
sslTruststoreType.description: The file format of the trust store file
